tips.title: Other ADs to check (part-dependent)
tips.text: The FAA DRS lists more ADs for the IO-540-G1C5 and -K1A5, but each one only applies if certain parts, serial numbers or dates match, so check them against the engine logbook at the annual: 2026-17-10 (piston pins), 2026-04-11 (connecting rods), 2022-16-03 (magnetos), 2017-16-11, 2012-19-01 (crankshafts), 2012-03-06 and 2009-02-03 (fuel servos), 2006-10-21 (ECi rods), 2005-19-11, 2005-12-06, 2004-10-14, 2004-05-24, 2003-14-03, 2002-19-03, 99-04-04 (Slick mags), 97-15-11, 96-23-03, 95-07-01, 83-22-04, 79-04-05, 78-23-10, 75-09-15, 75-08-09, 73-23-01, 66-20-04. Propeller ADs depend on the installed prop.
tips.note: Searched on the FAA DRS by model (A-9B, IO-540-G1C5, IO-540-K1A5). Superseded (historical) ADs are left out.

schedule.basis: Required within the preceding 12 calendar months (14 CFR 91.409(a)). Due at the end of the month.

14 CFR 91.409(b): required within each 100 hrs time in service when the aircraft carries any person (other than a crewmember) for hire, or is provided for flight instruction for hire. An annual also counts. Up to 10 hrs over only to reach a place where it can be done.
schedule.note: Conditional. The rule text names carrying persons for hire and flight instruction for hire; it does not mention towing. If the aircraft tows for hire, confirm with your IA or FSDO whether a 100-hour applies.

schedule.basis: Lycoming SB 480F: with a full-flow oil filter, every 50 hrs or 4 months, whichever comes first. With only an oil pressure screen, every 25 hrs or 4 months (clean the screen). First change at 25 hrs after new or overhaul.
schedule.note: Not yet known whether this engine has a spin-on filter or only a screen. If it’s a screen, edit this item to 25 hrs.

schedule.task: AD 2015-19-07: fuel injector lines & clamps inspection
schedule.basis: Applies to IO-540-G1C5 and -K1A5 with external fuel injector lines. Repeat within every 110 hrs time in service, after any maintenance that loosens or moves a fuel-line clamp, and after each overhaul (Lycoming MSB 342G).

schedule.task: AD 73-22-02: wing lift strut eye-fitting welds
schedule.basis: Applies to Models A-9, A-9A and A-9B. One-time: check for 360° welds at the P/N 10671 eye fittings on all four lift struts. If not sealed, check for water and corrosion, then weld. Record the compliance method.
Applies to IO-540 series engines (except -W). One-time records check for piston pins P/N LW-14077 bought Jun 18 – Aug 5, 1991, or an engine serial listed in Lycoming SB 501B. Replace affected pins.

Applies to IO-540 series except “5D” models, so both TCDS engines. Confirm hardened-steel oil pump impellers; sintered-iron or aluminum impellers must be replaced (at overhaul or pump removal per the AD). Record the compliance.
Applies to A-9, A-9A and A-9B that have the wing-strut carry-through tube running through the hopper. Inspect the fiberglass wrap; remove corrosion; replace tube P/N 11013 if past the limits.
schedule.note: Conditional: only if the carry-through tube runs through the hopper.

schedule.task: ELT inspection & battery (if an ELT is installed)
schedule.basis: 14 CFR 91.207(d): inspect within 12 calendar months. 91.207(c): replace or recharge the battery after 1 cumulative hr of use or at 50% of its useful life (date marked on the unit).
schedule.note: Conditional: 91.207(f)(9) exempts aircraft equipped to carry not more than one person (the TCDS lists 1 seat), and (f)(6) ag application flights. Track it if an ELT is installed.

schedule.basis: 14 CFR 91.413: an installed ATC transponder must be tested and inspected within the preceding 24 calendar months.
schedule.note: Conditional: only if a transponder is installed and used.

schedule.basis: 14 CFR 91.411: altimeter, static system and encoder tested within the preceding 24 calendar months to fly IFR in controlled airspace.

tips.title: Where’s the serial?
tips.text: On this machine the ID plate (tractor number, model, unit, engine and component codes) is on the operator platform / ROPS area: a yellow panel near the seat and fuel cap. A parts site also says the engine serial is stamped on the left side of the block above the oil filter, and that the model ID plate may be under the hood near the battery or on the dash cowl.
tips.note: The general locations come from a parts site (brokentractor.com), not the factory manual. Keep the tractor number, engine serial and PIN in the Vault, not in public fields.
